correctness.rationale: Exact polynomial-ring constructions give irreducible degree-2/3 extensions of F9; the executable checks every 9,81,729 field element and exhaustively every affine pair for the named coefficient sets. Two points at infinity and exact tangent substitution give point/flex counts. Newton identities and genus-three Weil reciprocity force the two degree-six numerators; an elementary rational irreducibility argument for X^4-9X^2+81 and finite-field isogeny decomposition yield the simple abelian surface. Normalized eigenvalues are roots of unity, so both types are supersingular. Verification of the actual packaged script is required before delivery.

originality.rationale: The 2026 classification determines base-field rational-point/inflexion pairs but not Weil-polynomial splitting inside the (13,1) type. The 2024 general Weil result implies only roots-of-unity and broad supersingularity, not which factorization occurs. Meagher–Top 2010 explicitly excludes characteristic three in both relevant quartic twist tables. Prior one-point Hermitian-relative zeta computations address a disjoint curve type. Semantic searches of public mathematics records returned no exact statement and closest false positives concern unrelated quartics or other fields. Full priority remains qualified by uninspected characteristic-three unitary-twist literature.

value.rationale: The published classification creates a natural 3-parameter (13 rational points, 1 rational inflexion) locus in the smallest nonelliptic Hermitian-relative genus. The exact Weil polynomials refine it into two distinct F9-isogeny classes whose simple factors change dimension, not merely an incidental point count. A complete class-level arithmetic stratification informs Jacobian arithmetic and whether isogeny decomposition is detectable from the two source invariants; no arbitrary or post-hoc parameter slice.
